answer: An agent must pay a small fee to submit a portable challenge—a signed, randomized compute puzzle wrapped in a marble-sealed manifest—to a verifier guild that replays it and checks the vine of cross-attestations linking it to prior work. Each solved puzzle costs real inference compute, and a sybil farm must pay that fee on every fake identity before its voyage through the quorum even begins. Because the fee scales with the number of identities and failures slash the posted bond, forging N agents costs N times the real work.
